title: What continuing education do Texas real estate agents and brokers need to renew?
description: TREC continuing education: 18 hours every two years with Legal Update I and II and 3 hours of contracts, the 6 hour broker course, SAE and the CE deferral.
shortAnswer: Texas real estate sales agents and brokers must complete 18 hours of continuing education approved by the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC) for each two-year license renewal. The 18 hours must include Legal Update I and Legal Update II (4 hours each) and 3 hours on real estate contracts, under 22 Texas Administrative Code section 535.92. Sponsoring brokers, designated brokers of sponsoring entities and delegated supervisors must include the 6 hour Broker Responsibility Course.
keyTakeaways: Sales agent and broker licenses are renewed every two years, and each renewal needs 18 hours of TREC-approved CE.
The fixed components are Legal Update I: Laws, Rules and Forms (4 hours), Legal Update II: Agency, Ethics and Hot Topics (4 hours), and 3 hours on real estate contracts; the rest are electives.
The 6 hour Broker Responsibility Course counts inside the 18 hours for brokers who sponsor agents, designated brokers of entities that sponsor agents, and delegated supervisors.
Sales agents renewing for the first time follow Sales Agent Apprentice Education (SAE) instead: 90 hours of qualifying courses plus Legal Update I and II, and these hours cannot be deferred.
Agents and brokers past their first renewal can pay a $200 CE deferral fee for 60 extra days to finish CE while staying active.
jurisdiction: United States (Texas): Texas Real Estate License Act (Occupations Code chapter 1101) and 22 Texas Administrative Code section 535.92
appliesTo: Real estate sales agents after their first renewal
Individual real estate brokers, including designated brokers of business entities
Delegated supervisors appointed by a broker
Sales agents in their first license period, under SAE requirements
TREC-approved continuing education providers, who report completions to TREC

sections.heading: How many CE hours do Texas real estate license holders need?

blocks.text: Texas license holders need 18 hours of continuing education for each renewal, and the license runs for two years. TREC's [sales agent renewal page](https://www.trec.texas.gov/renew-license/real-estate-sales-agent) states that a sales agent must renew every two years, and that TREC sends a renewal notice about 90 days before expiry.

The content of the 18 hours is fixed in rule. Section 535.92(a) of TREC's rules, published in the Texas Administrative Code ([22 TAC 535.92](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/22-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-535-92)), requires each renewal to include a four hour Legal Update I: Laws, Rules and Forms course, a four hour Legal Update II: Agency, Ethics and Hot Topics course, and three hours on the subject of real estate contracts from one or more Commission approved courses.

sections.heading: Who must take the Broker Responsibility Course?

blocks.text: The six hour Broker Responsibility Course is required for brokers who supervise others, and it counts toward the 18 hours rather than adding to them. Under section 535.92(a)(4) it applies to a license holder who sponsors one or more sales agents at any time during the current license period, who is the designated broker of a business entity that sponsors one or more sales agents, or who is a delegated supervisor under section 535.2(e).

TREC's [broker renewal page](https://www.trec.texas.gov/renew-license/real-estate-broker) shows the practical effect: for brokers the breakdown is 8 hours of Legal Update, 6 hours of Broker Responsibility, 3 hours of contracts and 1 hour of electives. A sales agent named as a delegated supervisor also takes the course, which agencies sometimes miss when they appoint team leads.

sections.heading: What do Texas sales agents need for their first renewal?

blocks.text: Sales agents renewing for the first time follow Sales Agent Apprentice Education (SAE) rather than the 18 hour CE rule. TREC's sales agent page lists a 30 hour Real Estate Brokerage course, 60 hours of qualifying education taken as two 30 hour courses from a list that includes Real Estate Finance, Real Estate Law and Residential Property Management, Advanced, and 8 hours of Legal Update I and II.

blocks.title: Primary text: TREC
blocks.text: "These hours cannot be deferred, so if you do not complete them in time for your renewal, your license expires."

TREC's answer to a related question summarizes the total: before a first renewal, the agent must have completed a total of 270 hours of qualifying course hours and the Legal Update I and II courses. Delegated supervisors in their first period must also complete the Broker Responsibility Course.

sections.heading: What happens if CE is not finished by the expiration date?

blocks.text: A license holder past the first renewal can pay a $200 CE deferral fee or renew in inactive status. According to TREC's [CE deferral article](https://www.trec.texas.gov/article/need-more-time-complete-ce-renew-here%E2%80%99s-what-do), paying the nonrefundable fee keeps the person active for 60 days beyond the expiration date to complete the required continuing education. The deferral is not available to sales agents in their first renewal period.

items: **Return from inactive:** a sales agent who goes inactive must take three hours of contract-related coursework to return to active status, and it counts toward the next renewal.
**Late renewal:** a license can be renewed up to six months after expiry; from six months to two years it must be reinstated; after two years the person must reapply and pass the exam.
**Repeat credit:** under section 535.92(h), TREC will not award credit for attending or instructing the same course more than once in a license period.

**Other credit routes:** up to four elective hours per license period for attending a full quarterly Commission meeting in person, and elective credit for qualifying courses of at least 30 classroom hours.

sections.heading: How should a Texas brokerage track CE for its agents?

blocks.text: TREC awards credit when it receives a course completion roster from the CE provider (section 535.92(b)), so the license holder search on TREC's website is the authoritative check of posted hours. A brokerage's own record should reconcile with it. The table below is an illustrative template, not a TREC form.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can map the written policies and procedures a Texas broker must maintain under section 535.2, such as those for sponsored agents' advertising, to outcomes that delegated supervisors are assessed on, complementing the Broker Responsibility Course. Changes announced in each Legal Update cycle can then be traced to the internal procedures they affect. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Do Texas real estate agents need Legal Update on their first renewal?
faqs.a: Yes. TREC states that sales agents renewing for the first time, who are under Sales Agent Apprentice Education, must complete Legal Update I and Legal Update II in addition to the SAE qualifying courses. The 3 hour contracts requirement belongs to the standard 18 hour CE rule that applies from the second renewal.

faqs.q: Can a Texas agent take the same CE course twice for credit?
faqs.a: No. Section 535.92(h) says TREC will not award credit to a license holder who attends or instructs the same course more than once during the current license period, or during the two years before a late renewal or return to active status.

faqs.q: Does a Texas broker need 24 hours if they also take the Broker Responsibility Course?
faqs.a: No. The six hour Broker Responsibility Course counts within the 18 hours. TREC's broker breakdown is 8 hours of Legal Update, 6 hours of Broker Responsibility, 3 hours of contracts and 1 hour of electives.

faqs.q: Can out-of-state CE count in Texas?
faqs.a: Possibly, as elective credit only. Under section 535.92(d), TREC may approve a course taken to meet another jurisdiction's CE requirements if the person held an active license there at the time, the course was approved there, completion is evidenced, and the person files a credit request with TREC.

factCheck.claim: Sales agents renew every two years; renewal notice about 90 days before expiry; 18 hours CE including Legal Update I and II (8 hours), 3 hours contract-related coursework and 7 elective hours; delegated supervisors take the 6 hour Broker Responsibility course; renewal up to six months after expiry, reinstatement to two years, then reapply and exam.

SAE for first renewal: 30 hour Real Estate Brokerage course, 60 hours (two 30 hour qualifying courses), 8 hours Legal Update I and II; SAE hours cannot be deferred; 270 total qualifying hours before first renewal; going inactive requires 3 hours contracts to return active.
Broker renewal: 8 hours Legal Update, 6 hour Broker Responsibility Course, 3 hours contracts, 1 hour elective; $200 CE deferral fee gives 60 extra days.
Sales agents (except first renewal period) and brokers may pay a nonrefundable $200 fee to remain active for 60 days beyond expiration to complete CE.

22 TAC 535.92(a): 18 hours with four hour Legal Update I: Laws, Rules and Forms, four hour Legal Update II: Agency, Ethics and Hot Topics, three hours contracts, six hour broker responsibility for sponsoring brokers, designated brokers of sponsoring entities and delegated supervisors under 535.2(e); (b) credit on receipt of provider roster; (d) out-of-state courses; (f) up to four hours for a Commission meeting; (h) no repeat credit; last amended effective 8/29/2023.
